Date: 2025-08-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Santos (Redwood SE), Samantha Reed (Lyra Head of Product), Dr. Naveen Kumar (Lyra ML Lead), Alex Torres (Eng Manager), Maya Chen (Security)
summary: Redwood demo of evaluation and quality monitoring features focused on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparison workflows. Customer is evaluating Redwood for a 6-week POC to monitor clinical triage prompts and ensure no regressions after model changes. Key concerns: data residency, SOC2/KMS, latency impact, and integration effort.
topics: Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate you making time. Uh, quick roll call - Jordan from Redwood, Marco from our SE team.
[00:12] Samantha Reed: Hi hi, Samantha here, thanks. Naveen, Alex and Maya from our side.
[00:20] Marco Santos: Great - before we jump in, quick agenda: we want to walk through Redwood's eval / quality monitoring features - prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons - and then show the Console and the API flows. We'll leave time for security questions. Sound good?
[00:38] Alex Torres: Yep sounds good. We're mainly curious about how we'd detect regressions after model updates and how noisy the alerts are.
[00:48] Jordan Lee: Totally. We'll demo both automated detection and manual evals, and how you can tie alerts to prompt sets and rerun baselines.
[00:57] Marco Santos: Ok opening the Redwood Console - you might see some UI artifacts, sorry if the consoel nav is a bit different - we recently updated the layout. So top-left is the Eval tab, where you create prompt sets.
[01:12] Marco Santos: Prompt sets are collections of prompts + expected outputs and scoring functions. For Lyra's clinical triage use case we'd recommend a mix of golden prompts, edge cases, and adversarial examples.
[01:26] Dr. Naveen Kumar: Quick question - can prompt sets include structured metadata, like patient age groups and consent flags?
[01:34] Marco Santos: Yes, you can attach tags and metadata to each example. The console supports filtering and slicing by tag, age group, intent, et cetera. That metadata also drives alerting and cohort-specific thresholds.
[01:48] Samantha Reed: Nice. We have strict regulatory constraints, so metadata and residency matters.
[01:54] Maya Chen: On that point, how does Redwood handle PII in eval datasets? We can't send PHI to hosted environments unless we have a contract.
[02:04] Jordan Lee: Good question. For POC we can set up a Private deployment or a Dedicated instance, and you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with KMS/HSM. We also support redaction tools in the eval pipeline; you can hash or mask fields before upload.
[02:20] Maya Chen: Great - can you send SOC2 docs and the security whitepaper?
[02:24] Jordan Lee: We'll send the SOC2 and the security whitepaper after this call.
[02:29] Marco Santos: Back to alerts - in the console you can configure regression alerts at the prompt-set level. We support both absolute thresholds and relative change detection (e.g., drop in pass rate by X% over baseline). We also do semantic similarity checks with embeddings to catch paraphrase regressions.
[02:46] Alex Torres: Embedding-based detection - is that configurable? Like what similarity metric and threshold?
[02:52] Marco Santos: Yes - default is cosine similarity on our embedding spec, threshold is configurable per prompt set. You can also choose fuzzy string metrics or exact match for deterministic checks.
[03:04] Dr. Naveen Kumar: For clinical language, exact match is often too brittle. Embedding similarity would help - how noisy is it in practice?
[03:11] Marco Santos: It depends on your pass/fail scoring function. We recommend combined heuristics: embedding similarity plus rule-based checks (e.g., deny patterns). That reduces false positives. You can tune with a small labeled validation set.
[03:25] Samantha Reed: Show us an example alert?
[03:29] Marco Santos: Sure - opening the Alerts panel. Here's a regression: 'triage severity drift' - pass rate dropped from 95% to 83% after a model patch. You'll see affected prompt IDs, sample inputs, reference outputs, and the model outputs.
[03:47] Jordan Lee: We also attach diff views and a suggested mitigation: rollback to previous model or pin to conservative variant. The alert shows confidence and suggested owner.
[03:56] Alex Torres: Does the alert link into our ticketing system? We use Jira.
[04:00] Marco Santos: Yes - you can push alerts into Jira, PagerDuty, or Slack. There's webhook integration too.
[04:07] Samantha Reed: What about A/B comparisons? We run small model rollout experiments.
[04:12] Marco Santos: The A/B flow in Console lets you run an experiment against two model variants. You can attach the same prompt set and compare metrics (pass rate, semantic score, latency, token cost). We'll show a live A/B comparison chart.
[04:27] Marco Santos: Here's an A/B run: baseline gpt-3-ish variant vs quantized variant - you can see tradeoffs: lower cost but slight drop in semantic score for some cohorts.
[04:39] Dr. Naveen Kumar: Do you do statistical significance calculations? We need to know if differences are meaningful for clinical thresholds.
[04:46] Marco Santos: Yes - we provide p-values and bootstrap confidence intervals for metrics across the prompt set. You can define your success criteria (e.g., no more than 2% drop in pass rate at 95% CI).
[04:59] Alex Torres: Integration - can we run evals via API in CI? We want automated regression detection on deploy.
[05:05] Marco Santos: Absolutely. The Evaluation API supports uploading prompt sets, running jobs, and getting structured results. Many customers wire it into CI to block deploys if regression alerts trigger.
[05:15] Jordan Lee: I'll note that our SDK also supports streaming of intermediate outputs so you can do early aborts if a run is clearly failing.
[05:23] Samantha Reed: About latency - will eval instrumentation add latency to our live endpoints?
[05:28] Marco Santos: No, evals are separate jobs. For production monitoring we use sampling and non-blocking tracing. There's a small overhead for tracing calls if you enable request-level telemetry, but it's configurable and usually below 5% CPU overhead.
[05:43] Maya Chen: For data residency, can the evals run in our VPC?
[05:47] Jordan Lee: Yes - for Private or Dedicated we can run evals in-customer VPC. For hosted evals we support region pinning and don't persist raw inputs unless you opt in.
[05:58] Alex Torres: Can you show the prompt-set creation flow?
[06:02] Marco Santos: Sure - creating a prompt set: name, description, tags, expected outputs, scoring function. You can upload via CSV or API. We have a sample template that includes columns: prompt_id, input_text, expected_output, tags, cohort.
[06:18] Marco Santos: Here's a sample prompt with expected output for triage severity. You can attach multiple reference outputs and set scoring to 'semantic similarity' with threshold 0.85.
[06:30] Dr. Naveen Kumar: Multiple references would really help capture acceptable variance.
[06:34] Marco Santos: Exactly. And you can weight references to bias toward conservative outputs.
[06:40] Samantha Reed: For A/B rollout, can we tie it to traffic split and then backtest on historical logs?
[06:48] Marco Santos: You can point the compare job at historical logs; it will replay inputs under both model variants and compute diffs. That helps you predict user impact before live traffic.
[06:58] Alex Torres: That replay sounds useful. Is the replay deterministic? For non-deterministic models we may get variance.
[07:05] Marco Santos: We capture seeds and runtime config when replaying. There's still stochasticity, but the analytics account for variance in the significance tests.
[07:14] Samantha Reed: Switching to success criteria: we need 95% pass on golden set and no PII leakage. Can we encode PII checks?
[07:23] Marco Santos: Yes - we have a PII detection policy you can run as a scoring function. It flags likely PHI or SSN patterns, and you can make that a hard fail to trigger alerts.
[07:34] Maya Chen: Can those PII detectors be customer-controlled? We want to add custom regexes and a denylist.
[07:40] Marco Santos: Yep - custom detectors and denylists are supported; you can upload them via API or manage in the Console.
[07:47] Samantha Reed: How are regression alert thresholds configured? Global or per-prompt-set?
[07:52] Marco Santos: Per-prompt-set and per-cohort. So you might tolerate a 4% drop on broad coverage prompts but set a 1% tolerance on critical clinical prompts.
[08:02] Dr. Naveen Kumar: Let's talk about metric drift detection - do you track embedding drift over time?
[08:08] Marco Santos: We do. There's a drift dashboard that tracks mean-embedding shift, token distribution, model confidence histogram, and we can auto-create alerts on z-score thresholds.
[08:18] Alex Torres: Any examples of false positives from those drift alerts?
[08:22] Marco Santos: We see false positives when upstream data distribution changes - e.g., seasonal language shifts. That's why we recommend cohorted thresholds and a short manual review flow inside alerts.
[08:34] Jordan Lee: Quick plug - Redwood Optimize will give recommendations for quantization and batching if you want to shift to a cheaper variant while preserving metrics.
[08:43] Samantha Reed: We will definitely need cost estimates.
[08:46] Jordan Lee: We'll include a cost/latency breakdown in the follow-up spreadsheet.
[08:50] Marco Santos: Now jumping to the API demo - here is an API call to create a prompt set programmatically. I'll paste a curl example.
[08:59] Marco Santos: (reads) curl -X POST /v1/evals -d '@promptset.csv' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' - you get back a job ID and can poll results.
[09:12] Alex Torres: Is there rate limiting for eval jobs?
[09:15] Marco Santos: We have quotas for hosted plans, but Dedicated/Private can set higher throughput. For POC we'll give you trial capacity.
[09:24] Dr. Naveen Kumar: Regarding model variants and pinning - if a rollout goes bad, can requests automatically failover to previous variant?
[09:32] Marco Santos: Yes - we support automatic fallback policies by route or by percentage. The routing layer can do health checks and instant fallback.
[09:40] Samantha Reed: For the POC, we want to run weekly regression scans and get an automated report. Can Redwood schedule that?
[09:46] Jordan Lee: Yes, scheduled runs, and you can export reports to S3 or push to your BI. For the POC we'll set up weekly scheduled scans.
[09:55] Maya Chen: How long does it take to onboard our first prompt set?
[09:58] Marco Santos: From upload to first results is typically minutes to an hour depending on size. Small sets (<500 prompts) return in minutes.
[10:08] Samantha Reed: Are there examples or templates for clinical prompt sets?
[10:11] Marco Santos: We have industry templates; I will share a sample template for healthcare triage.
[10:17] Jordan Lee: Also sharing a demo recording and a benchmark spreadsheet after the call.
[10:22] Alex Torres: On the audit/compliance side, does the eval pipeline preserve logs for X days?
[10:27] Marco Santos: Retention is configurable. We store audit logs with SSO identity and action metadata; default is 90 days for hosted, but enterprise retention can be extended.
[10:36] Maya Chen: Do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC?
[10:39] Jordan Lee: Yes - SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. We'll include the docs.
[10:46] Dr. Naveen Kumar: We may want to run some adversarial prompts - can we automate generation?
[10:51] Marco Santos: You can plug in your generators or use Redwood's adversarial harness to create paraphrases, typos, and edge cases. It will add those to the prompt set automatically.
[11:02] Samantha Reed: What's the expected engineering effort to run the POC?
[11:06] Jordan Lee: For a standard POC we usually need: sample prompt set, small historical logs for replay, and one infra contact for VPC/KMS if private. The Redwood team will help configure. Typical ramp is 1-2 weeks to start seeing meaningful reports.
[11:20] Alex Torres: Good. Timeline looks OK.
[11:23] Marco Santos: Quick demo of the alert triage UI - you can assign owner, add notes, attach a Jira ticket, and mark as mitigated.
[11:33] Samantha Reed: Can we customize the alert severity labels?
[11:37] Marco Santos: Yes - you can map internal severity taxonomy to Redwood's alert severities.
[11:42] Jordan Lee: Any other security concerns?
[11:44] Maya Chen: We need to know about KMS key rotation policies and proof of key separation.
[11:50] Jordan Lee: We support customer-managed keys and hardware-backed HSMs. Rotation policy is customer-defined; we'll document separation of duties in the whitepaper.
[11:59] Alex Torres: A little worried about telemetry overhead again - does running sampling reduce observability?
[12:04] Marco Santos: You can control sampling rate per route; high-sensitivity routes can be 100% sampled while others are low. The analytics pipeline can still surface system-level metrics.
[12:15] Samantha Reed: For our success criteria: 95% pass on golden, false positive rate <2% on PII detectors, and rollout failover time <60s. Can Redwood measure those?
[12:24] Marco Santos: Yes - we can compute those metrics and put them on the POC dashboard.
[12:30] Jordan Lee: Ok let's walk through a hypothetical POC run: week 0 onboarding and dataset upload, week 1 initial baseline, weeks 2-3 A/B experiments and replay, week 4-6 monitoring and decision.
[12:44] Dr. Naveen Kumar: Sounds reasonable. Who will own the POC from Redwood?
[12:48] Jordan Lee: Jordan AE will coordinate and Marco will own technical onboarding.
[12:52] Samantha Reed: Any blockers for legal? We might need a DPA and subprocessor list.
[12:57] Jordan Lee: We'll include DPA and subprocessor list in the follow-up package.
[13:02] Maya Chen: Also need vulnerability scan report and SOC2 attestations.
[13:07] Jordan Lee: Noted.
[13:09] Alex Torres: For A/B reporting, can we export raw per-prompt outputs for in-house evaluation?
[13:15] Marco Santos: Yes - exports to S3 or direct download. You can also request hashed outputs if you don't want raw text exported.
[13:24] Samantha Reed: Client-side question - will Redwood store our model weights or just host endpoints?
[13:29] Marco Santos: Depends on deployment. For hosted we host models but we separate tenancy. For Private/Dedicated you can bring your own models and they never leave your environment unless you opt in.
[13:40] Dr. Naveen Kumar: For evaluation scoring functions can we plug in custom Python logic?
[13:46] Marco Santos: We support custom scoring via webhooks or serverless evaluators. For security you can host the scorer in your VPC and Redwood will call it during evaluation.
[13:58] Samantha Reed: That would be ideal, we want to use our clinical scoring function.
[14:01] Marco Santos: Great. I'll include an integration guide.
[14:05] Jordan Lee: Moving toward next steps - we'll send pricing, SOC2, security docs, the sample prompt set, and a POC plan.
[14:13] Samantha Reed: Perfect. Can you also share a sample Jira integration config?
[14:17] Marco Santos: Yep.
[14:19] Alex Torres: Any concerns about tokenization differences across model variants affecting scoring?
[14:25] Marco Santos: We account for tokenization differences in the cost and length distributions in reports. For semantic scoring tokenization matters less because embeddings normalize across tokens, but deterministic rules may be impacted.
[14:37] Samantha Reed: Ok wrapping up: can we capture the explicit POC success criteria in email?
[14:42] Jordan Lee: Yes we'll capture the 95% pass rate, <2% PII false positive, and <60s failover in the POC doc.
[14:50] Maya Chen: Thanks.
[14:51] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials and set up the POC workspace.
[14:58] Samantha Reed: Appreciate it, speak soon.
[15:01] Meeting end: call disconnected. Note: partial transcription errors likely in product names and minor typos.
